classification.difficultyReason: Standardise a contextual measurement, then use symmetry and a table complement for a negative z-score.

content.prompt: A machine produces cylindrical pipes. The mean of the diameters of the pipes is 7.00 cm and the standard deviation is 0.03 cm. Assuming a normal distribution, what is the probability that a randomly chosen pipe has a diameter less than 6.95 cm? Use the standard normal table, rounding the z-score to 2 decimal places. Give the probability to 4 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Let $X$ be the pipe diameter in centimetres.
$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{6.95-7.00}{0.03}\\z&=-\frac53\\z&\approx-1.67\end{aligned}$$
Using symmetry and the standard normal table:
$$\begin{aligned}P(X<6.95)&=P\left(Z<-\frac53\right)\\P(X<6.95)&\approx P(Z<-1.67)\\P(X<6.95)&\approx P(Z>1.67)\\P(X<6.95)&\approx1-0.9525\\P(X<6.95)&\approx0.0475.\end{aligned}$$
